prompts.text: What's a photograph you value because of what happened just outside the frame?
Describe discovering an old picture that reminded you of a detail you'd forgotten.
Keep a small printed album or organise your favourite pictures into digital collections?
You can preserve five ordinary moments from this year in a time capsule. What would you photograph?
People often treasure unplanned pictures more than perfectly posed ones.
Not every meaningful experience needs to be photographed.
Which kind of moment makes you reach for your camera almost automatically?
Recall seeing a familiar place in an old photo and noticing what has changed.
You're asked to make a photo essay about an ordinary week without showing any faces. What would you include?
Capture a daily detail for one month or revisit the same location once each season?
What's the easiest way for you to remember a task that isn't urgent?
Tell me about creating a simple reminder system after forgetting something small.
Write a short daily list or keep one calendar for everything that has a date?
You've got three free hours and several unrelated errands. What would help you choose the order?
Some tasks become overwhelming because people carry them around mentally rather than writing them down.
A system that takes more effort than the chores it tracks isn't a useful system.
Which small organisational trick has saved you more trouble than you expected?
Recall a day when planning ahead left you with an unexpected pocket of free time.
You have an important appointment and a few optional tasks nearby. How would you avoid rushing?
Group similar tasks together or handle each one as soon as it appears?
What's something you enjoy about travelling through your city without being the person driving?
Describe overhearing a harmless conversation during a journey that stayed with you.
Sit by a bus window and observe the streets or spend the ride reading?
A usual route is closed for a day. How would you decide whether to explore an alternative?
Commuting can make people surprisingly familiar with places they've never actually stopped to visit.
The best route isn't always the one that saves the most minutes.
Which view along a familiar journey do you still look for?
Recall noticing a change to a street you hadn't walked along for months.
You have the choice between a direct but dull journey and a slightly longer scenic one. What would guide you?
Listen to a podcast during transit or spend the time thinking without headphones?
What's a comfortable piece of clothing you return to more often than you planned?
Tell me about finding an item you liked after years of thinking that style wasn't for you.
Keep a small wardrobe of versatile favourites or enjoy changing your style regularly?
You're packing for a three-day visit with unpredictable weather. Which practical items come first?
People often express personal style through small repeated choices rather than dramatic outfits.
Comfort and good presentation don't have to be competing goals.
Which colour do you enjoy wearing even when it isn't fashionable?
Recall someone complimenting a garment because they remembered the story behind it.
You can repair or alter one old piece of clothing you still love. What would you change?
Find a dependable tailor or learn a few basic clothing repairs yourself?
What's a useful thing you learnt from spending time with a neighbour?
Describe a small local event that made an area feel more welcoming.
Join a neighbourhood clean-up or help organise a relaxed community gathering?
A new resident asks how people usually meet one another nearby. What would you recommend?
A sense of belonging often develops through repeated ordinary encounters.
Community involvement doesn't require becoming close friends with everyone.
Which shared resource would make everyday life easier in your area?
Recall somebody in your neighbourhood offering unexpected help with a practical problem.
Your building creates a noticeboard where residents can exchange useful information. What categories should it have?
Share extra books through a small library or organise a tool-lending shelf?
How do you decide when to put your phone away for a while?
Tell me about an afternoon that felt longer because you spent less time checking notifications.
Keep only essential notifications or set aside a specific period for checking messages?
You plan a relaxed day in a place with poor mobile reception. What would you enjoy doing differently?
Digital conveniences sometimes create habits people never deliberately chose.
Being reachable doesn't mean needing to reply immediately to every harmless update.
What everyday activity would you enjoy more if your phone weren't within reach?
Recall a time a technology problem led you to rediscover an older way of doing something.
You're helping somebody new to smartphones set up a calmer home screen. What would you prioritise?
Read on a dedicated e-reader or open a physical book when you want a break from apps?
Which plant or tree do you enjoy seeing change through the year?
Describe successfully growing something you didn't initially know how to care for.
Keep a few hardy houseplants or grow simple herbs in containers?
You inherit a small balcony with enough sunlight for only a few pots. What would you plant?
Looking after a living thing can make small changes over time easier to notice.
A modest garden deserves appreciation even if it never produces much food.
What have you learnt from trying to care for a plant that struggled?
Recall visiting a garden that made you want to try growing something at home.
A friend gives you a plant without care instructions. How would you find out what it needs?
Watch seedlings grow from the beginning or look after an established plant with a story?
What's a kind of book you enjoy returning to even after you know how it ends?
Tell me about reading something that made an ordinary situation feel newly interesting.
Read a few pages every evening or settle into longer sessions when you have free time?
You visit a bookshop with a small budget and no particular title in mind. How do you choose?
Reading habits can shift with people's routines without changing their love of stories.
A short book that stays with you is worth more than a long book you struggle to finish.
Which non-fiction subject would you explore if you could find a beginner-friendly book about it?
Recall someone recommending reading material at exactly the right moment for you.
A neighbourhood book club asks you to suggest a low-pressure first meeting. What would you plan?
Discuss one book together or exchange brief recommendations and read independently?
What's a harmless personal tradition that makes an ordinary week feel special?
Describe a recurring activity that began accidentally but became something you looked forward to.
Reserve one evening for a favourite hobby or keep a flexible afternoon for spontaneous plans?
You want to begin a weekly ritual that costs almost nothing. What might you try?
People sometimes measure a satisfying week through moments that never appear on a work schedule.
A tradition doesn't have to be old to be meaningful.
Which part of the week has its own particular feeling for you?
Recall a little routine you shared with someone that continued after your schedules changed.
Your usual weekend activity becomes unavailable. What would be a suitable alternative with a similar mood?
Plan a regular quiet breakfast or take the same relaxed walk every weekend?
What's one small thing about your daily life that you're grateful has become easier?
Tell me about looking back on an ordinary problem you once found difficult and realising you've adapted.
Record a few highlights at the end of each month or rely on memories and conversations?
You write a letter about your present routine to open five years from now. What detail would you describe?
Progress can be hard to notice when it arrives through dozens of small adjustments.
A life can become richer without becoming busier.
Which ordinary activity helps you recognise that you're doing better than you were a year ago?
Recall a simple day that taught you something about what you genuinely enjoy.
You have to recommend one realistic change for somebody seeking a calmer week. What would you suggest?
Keep a brief journal of ordinary moments or collect one meaningful object from each season?
